newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bosnian Serb on trial in Germany for war crimes.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb on trial in Germany for war crimes.

text.p: A 34-year-old Bosnian Serb was charged by German prosecutors with aiding murder and genocide on Tuesday at the start of the first war crimes trial in Germany since the Nuremberg tribunal more than 50 years ago.

German federal prosecutors, who took on the case because of overload at the United Nations war crimes tribunal in the Hague, said Novislav Djajic took part in a June 1992 raid in which 14 Moslem men were killed and 15 others taken prisoner. The 15 were never seen again.
Prosecutors told the court that Djajic had known the Moslems would be shot.
Djajic, who entered Germany in 1993, was arrested in January 1996. A second Bosnian Serb, Nicola Jorgic, will soon face trial in Duesseldorf on similar charges.
"It is a mystery to me why this tribunal has been set up," said Djajic's lawyer Wolfgang Dingfelder, whose request on Tuesday to have the case dismissed was rejected by the court.
"It is my understanding that (The Hague) has enough capacity for this case. The reasons they did not take it are unknown."

Although the alleged offences were not committed in Germany, the men are being tried there under a passage of international law which says the perpetrators of genocide should not receive shelter anywhere and can be tried abroad.
Much of the prosecutor's case revolves around the testimony of one survivor of the massacre. A total of 27 witnesses are expected to testify and a ruling could be reached by April.
German prosecutors are investigating 48 other people suspected of war crimes in former Yugoslavia.
Germany's Nuremberg trials of Nazi leaders, conducted by judges and prosecutors from the four Allied victors, introduced the words "genocide" and "crimes aganst humanity" to the world's vocabulary.
Twelve men, including air force chief Hermann Goering, were sentenced to death by hanging. Seven received long prison sentences and three were acquitted.
